1. No, I would not perform rifampicin drug-resistance testing on this patient's initial diagnostic specimen. The Xpert MTB/RIF test has already detected rifampicin resistance, so further testing would not provide additional useful information.

2. I would send a mycobacterial culture on this patient after the initial Xpert MTB/RIF test, as it is a confirmatory test for TB diagnosis and can provide additional information on drug susceptibility. This is especially important since the Xpert MTB/RIF test has a high false-positive rate for rifampicin resistance.

3. Assuming the initial test confirms drug-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis, I would start the patient on a 6-month treatment regimen with the following phases and dosing schedule:
   (a) The treatment regimen would have two phases: an intensive phase (2 months) and a continuation phase (4 months).
   (b) During the intensive phase, the patient would take isoniazid (H), rifampicin (R), pyrazinamide (Z), and ethambutol (E) daily for 2 months, with the following dosing schedule: H 5 mg/kg, R 10 mg/kg, Z 15-20 mg/kg, and E 15-20 mg/kg, taken once daily. During the continuation phase, the patient would take H and R daily for 4 months, with the same dosing schedule as in the intensive phase.
